newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine sugar output seen up 13 pct in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Argentine sugar output seen up 13 pct in 1997/98.

text.p: Argentina's 1997/98 sugar crop, which is just beginning to be harvested, should produce 13 percent more than last year and make imports unnecessary, an Argentine Sugar Producers' Association analyst said Monday.
"No imports are foreseen," the association's Eduardo Oliver Muro told Reuters, "The canes are in good shape and output should rise by about 13 percent."
But he added that sudden frosts could always confound optimistic forecasts.
Last season's output totaled 1.29 million tonnes, of which 1.19 million tonnes were white sugar.
The first harvesting has already started in Tucuman province, but the whole national crop will not be collected until November.

Argentine domestic consumption is about 1.2 million tonnes of white sugar a year. The country is traditionally a modest net exporter, but occasionally imports from neighboring Brazil when its harvest is bad.
Argentina has an annual export quota of 70,000 tonnes of raw sugar for the U.S. market.
Argentina's sugar exports reached a peak of 791,000 tonnes, mainly of refined white sugar, in 1983.
